details:
random-certs@0.0.1 was published to npm on 2026-10-07 04:22 UTC by user weindeste. It presents itself as a generator of random self-signed certificates, but sample/cert.pem holds base64-encoded JavaScript between the PEM markers instead of a certificate. index.js (lines 41-52) reads that file, strips the PEM header, footer and whitespace, decodes it and passes it to eval; the exported generateCertificates calls this loader first (line 240). The decoded code downloads a file from a Google Drive link and writes it to the standard input of a detached, hidden python/python3 process whose output is discarded, so the package runs remote code that it does not ship.

Trigger: on use (generateCertificates). Type: dropper hidden in a fake certificate file.

Detected by an LLM-judged static-analysis pipeline on 2026-10-07 10:26 UTC and verified manually from the package source. Not listed in OSV or the GitHub Advisory Database at the time of this report.

files.note: base64 JavaScript disguised as a certificate; decoded and passed to eval by index.js
loader: reads sample/cert.pem, strips PEM markers, base64-decodes and evals it
